title: Want your AI chats to stay private? Brave TEEs up end-to-end encryption
key_facts: Brave Software has connected its Leo AI assistant to Z.ai's GLM 5.3 Flash under end-to-end encryption, using NEAR AI's trusted execution environment (TEE).
A prompt is encrypted on the device, sent using Oblivious HTTP, and forwarded by Brave's AI Gateway to the TEE without the user's IP address.
After Brave verifies the enclave's attestation, the browser encrypts the query with a key bound to the TEE; the TEE decrypts it, runs the model and returns an encrypted response.
NEAR AI's pipeline uses Intel TDX and Nvidia Confidential Compute; it keeps Brave from knowing what was asked and NEAR AI from knowing who asked during the network hop.
Leo can still search through the Brave Search API from inside the TEE, which keeps the user's IP address out of the picture.
Brendan Eich, Brave's co-founder and chief executive, said too much AI 'still runs on trust me bro promises'.
The implementation is incomplete: Brave intends to move verification into the browser, publish a log of TEE keys and provide enclave attestation for the exact model weights.
Apple, AWS, Google, Nvidia and Microsoft have some form of private cloud compute for AI; running an open weight model on local hardware is another route to privacy.
quote_evidence: Brave Software has set up a secure space so those using its browser can converse with the company's AI assistant in private.

The implementation isn't quite complete: Brave intends to work on moving the verification step into the browser and to publish a log of TEE keys, and to provide enclave attestation for exact model weights loaded into memory, among other things.
AI has raised the stakes, yet too much of it still runs on 'trust me bro' promises, often at the user's expense.
why_it_matters_hint: A mainstream browser offers a verifiable private channel to an AI assistant at a time when agents ask for broad access to personal data.
event_date: article 16 Oct 2026; launch date not stated
notes: Design claims are Brave's and NEAR AI's; The Register notes it is unfinished.
